summary: The risk-history chart in the customer drawer (views/details.js): the customer's last 30 event scores as a smoothed neutral line with level-coloured dots, drawn over faint bands for LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH and CRITICAL. It uses `responsive`, `linear`, `monotonePath` and `LEVEL_COLORS` from charts/core.js, the clip-path reveal from motion.js and the shared tooltip.

notes.text: Header comment: one customer's risk across their recent events, drawn over bands for the engine's four levels.
Imports: escaping and date formatting from dom.js, `clipReveal` for the entrance, the shared tooltip, and the core helpers including `LEVEL_COLORS`.
`riskLine(el, points, options)`. `points` is the customer's `risk_history` from the API: up to 30 recent events, oldest first, each with `timestamp`, `risk_score`, `risk_level` and `event_id`.
A unique id for this chart's clip path.
Draws through `responsive`, so the chart fits the drawer's width and redraws on resize.
Resolves the four level colours from CSS for the band and dot fills, which are SVG attributes.
Padding (28 px on the left for the band labels) and the inner plot size.
The x scale maps an event's index to a pixel; `Math.max(..., 1)` keeps the domain non-zero when there is only one point.
The y scale is fixed at 0–100, the full score range, and inverted so higher scores sit higher. A fixed scale keeps the bands in the same place for every customer.
The four level bands as score ranges, matching the 30/60/80 thresholds.
The smoothed line through every score. The monotone curve matters here: a curve that overshoots could poke into a higher band and suggest a level the customer never reached.
Opens the SVG with `role="img"` and an accessible label.
A clip path with a full-size rect; the entrance animation grows its width to reveal the line from the left.

For each band, a rect from its upper to its lower boundary tinted in that level's colour at 5.5% opacity, plus a label with the band's lower bound (0, 30, 60, 80) on the left axis, just above the boundary.
Inside the clipped group, the line itself in neutral grey (`--t2`); the line carries no colour so that colour on this chart only ever means risk level.

A dot per event, filled with its level's colour; HIGH and CRITICAL events (score 60 and up) get a larger radius so they stand out, and a ring in the panel background colour separates each dot from the line. `data-i` links the dot back to its point for the tooltip.
Instead of crowded dates, the x axis simply says 'older' on the left and 'latest' on the right; exact times are in the tooltip.
Closes the SVG template.
Keeps a reference to the SVG.
One delegated `pointermove` listener: if the pointer isn't over a dot (`closest("circle[data-i]")`), it hides the tooltip and stops.
Looks up the point and shows its event id and time as the title, then its score and level. The closing `});` ends the handler.
Hides the tooltip when the pointer leaves the chart.

First draw only: the clip-path reveal grows the clip rect from 0 to the full width over 1.1 s, so the line and dots sweep in from the left; the bands sit outside the clipped group and are visible straight away.
Closes the `responsive` callback and `riskLine`.
